title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul, called to be an apostle
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, called to be an apostle
questions.explanation: Paul introduces himself at the beginning of the chapter as stated in 1 Corinthians 1:1.

questions.question: To whom is the letter of 1 Corinthians addressed?
options: The church of God in Ephesus
The church of God in Corinth
The church of God in Rome
The church of God in Galatia
questions.correctAnswer: The church of God in Corinth
questions.explanation: The letter is specifically addressed to the church of God which is at Corinth as noted in 1 Corinthians 1:2.

questions.question: What does Paul wish for the recipients of the letter?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses his wish for grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ in 1 Corinthians 1:3.

questions.question: What does Paul thank God for concerning the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul thanks God for the grace of God which is given to the Corinthians as indicated in 1 Corinthians 1:4.

questions.question: In what areas are the Corinthians enriched?
questions.explanation: The text states that in everything they are enriched by Him, in all utterance and in all knowledge, according to 1 Corinthians 1:5.

questions.question: What was confirmed in the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: The testimony of Christ was confirmed in the Corinthians as stated in 1 Corinthians 1:6.

questions.question: What are the Corinthians waiting for?
options: The coming of the Holy Spirit
The coming of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The coming of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the Corinthians are waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ in 1 Corinthians 1:7.

questions.question: What will the Lord Jesus Christ do for the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 1:8, the Lord Jesus Christ shall also confirm them unto the end.

questions.question: What is said about God in relation to the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: The verse states that God is faithful, by whom the Corinthians were called unto the fellowship of His Son, as noted in 1 Corinthians 1:9.

questions.question: What does Paul beseech the brethren to do?
questions.explanation: Paul beseeches the brethren to all speak the same thing and to have no divisions among them as stated in 1 Corinthians 1:10.

questions.question: Who declared that there are contentions among the brethren?
questions.explanation: It has been declared unto Paul by them which are of the house of Chloe that there are contentions among the brethren, according to 1 Corinthians 1:11.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was called to be an apostle through the will of God.
questions.explanation: This is stated explicitly in 1 Corinthians 1:1.

questions.question: True or False: The letter is addressed only to the apostles.
questions.explanation: The letter is addressed to the church of God at Corinth, not just to the apostles, as noted in 1 Corinthians 1:2.

questions.question: True or False: The Corinthians have been enriched in all utterance and knowledge.
questions.explanation: This fact is mentioned in 1 Corinthians 1:5 where it states they are enriched in all utterance and knowledge.

questions.question: True or False: Paul does not mention any divisions in the church.
questions.explanation: Paul explicitly mentions contentions and divisions among the brethren in 1 Corinthians 1:10-11.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 1:12, which groups do some believers claim to belong to?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:12 states, 'Now this I say, that every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 1:13 promise will happen if someone considers Christ divided?
options: It is a misguided division since Christ is not divided
They will be baptized in the name of Paul
They will be crucified for their beliefs
They will receive wisdom from the world
questions.correctAnswer: It is a misguided division since Christ is not divided
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:13 asks, 'Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?' indicating that Christ is not divided and such divisions are incorrect.

questions.question: Why does Paul thank God that he baptized few people, according to 1 Corinthians 1:14-15?
options: Lest anyone should say that he baptized in his own name
Because he wanted Apollos to baptize more
Because he was busy preaching elsewhere
questions.correctAnswer: Lest anyone should say that he baptized in his own name
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:14-15 states Paul thanks God that he baptized none but Crispus and Gaius, 'Lest any should say that I had baptized in mine own name.'

questions.question: How do 1 Corinthians 1:17 and 1 Corinthians 1:18 connect in Paul's mission and message?
options: Paul was sent to preach the gospel, not to baptize, because the preaching of the cross is the power of God
Paul was sent to baptize many, but the cross was foolishness
Paul preached wisdom of words to make the cross effective
Paul rejected baptism in favor of philosophy
questions.correctAnswer: Paul was sent to preach the gospel, not to baptize, because the preaching of the cross is the power of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:17 says Christ sent Paul not to baptize but to preach, and 1 Corinthians 1:18 explains preaching the cross is the power of God to believers.

questions.question: What practical lesson about divisions in the church can be learned from 1 Corinthians 1:10-12?
options: Christians should be united in mind and judgment to avoid contentions
It is acceptable to follow different leaders for personal preference
Divisions are signs of spiritual growth
questions.correctAnswer: Christians should be united in mind and judgment to avoid contentions
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:10-11 shows Paul urging believers to speak the same thing and avoid divisions, as contentions had been reported.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 1:19-20 describe God's approach to worldly wisdom?
options: God will destroy the wisdom of the wise and make the understanding of the prudent foolish
God will reward the wise and prudent
God encourages worldly wisdom as a path to faith
God is indifferent to human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: God will destroy the wisdom of the wise and make the understanding of the prudent foolish
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:19-20 quotes scripture saying God will destroy the wisdom of the wise and bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 1:21 indicate about God's method of salvation?
options: God uses the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe
God relies on human wisdom to save the world
God requires signs and wonders for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God uses the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:21 states that God, because the world did not know Him by wisdom, was pleased to save believers through the foolishness of preaching.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 1:22, what do Jews and Greeks respectively seek?
options: Jews require a sign, and Greeks seek after wisdom
Jews seek wisdom, and Greeks require signs
Both Jews and Greeks seek after power
Both Jews and Greeks require miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Jews require a sign, and Greeks seek after wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:22 clearly states, 'For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom.'

questions.question: What is the significance of Paul baptizing the household of Stephanas mentioned in 1 Corinthians 1:16?
options: It shows Paul’s selective baptism to avoid personal glorification
Paul baptized many to gain followers
Stephanas was the only believer in Corinth
Baptism was required before hearing the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Paul’s selective baptism to avoid personal glorification
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:16 says Paul baptized the household of Stephanas and some others, but he emphasizes he did not baptize many, to avoid anyone saying it was in his own name.

questions.question: How does Paul’s statement in 1 Corinthians 1:9 about God’s faithfulness encourage practical Christian living?
options: It assures believers they are called into fellowship with Jesus Christ and can trust God’s faithfulness
It warns believers they must earn their salvation
It emphasizes human wisdom over divine faithfulness
It encourages isolation from fellow believers
questions.correctAnswer: It assures believers they are called into fellowship with Jesus Christ and can trust God’s faithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:9 says, 'God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord,' encouraging trust and unity.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 1:7 say about the spiritual gifts of the believers?
options: They do not lack any gift and are waiting for the coming of Christ
They have few gifts and must earn more
They only have gifts from Paul
They are to reject gifts until Christ returns
questions.correctAnswer: They do not lack any gift and are waiting for the coming of Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:7 states the believers are not lacking in any gift and are waiting for the coming of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Why does Paul emphasize not baptizing many in 1 Corinthians 1:14-17 in relation to preaching?
options: To ensure the focus remains on preaching the gospel, not on baptism or human leaders
To promote Apollos as the main baptizer
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure the focus remains on preaching the gospel, not on baptism or human leaders
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 1:14-17, Paul highlights that he baptized few to prevent anyone from claiming allegiance to him and emphasizes that Christ sent him to preach, not to baptize.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 1:8 connect faithfulness with being blameless at the coming of Christ?
options: God will confirm believers to the end so they may be blameless on Christ’s day
Believers must be perfect without God’s help
questions.correctAnswer: God will confirm believers to the end so they may be blameless on Christ’s day
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:8 states God will confirm believers unto the end, so they may be blameless on the day of Christ Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 1:18 teaches that the preaching of the cross is foolishness to those who are saved.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:18 says the preaching of the cross is foolishness to those who perish, but to those who are saved it is the power of God.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 1:13, Paul was crucified for the believers.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:13 asks rhetorically, 'was Paul crucified for you?' showing that Paul was not crucified for believers; Christ was.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 1.

questions.question: What do we preach according to 1 Corinthians 1:23?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:23 states, 'But we preach Christ crucified...', indicating that the central message is about Christ's crucifixion.

questions.question: To whom is Christ the power and wisdom of God according to 1 Corinthians 1:24?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:24 says, 'But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 1:25 suggest about the foolishness of God?
options: It is equal to men’s wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:25 states, 'Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men...', showing that God's wisdom surpasses human understanding.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 1:26, who are not many of the called?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:26 mentions, 'For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.'

questions.question: What does God choose to confound the wise according to 1 Corinthians 1:27?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:27 states, 'But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise...', indicating God's choice of the foolish to challenge human wisdom.

questions.question: What should no flesh do in God's presence according to 1 Corinthians 1:29?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:29 says, 'That no flesh should glory in his presence.', emphasizing that human pride is not acceptable before God.

questions.question: What does 'wisdom' in 1 Corinthians 1:30 refer to in Greek?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 1:30, the Greek word for 'wisdom' is 'Sophia', which signifies a deep understanding and insight.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in 1 Corinthians 1:27 where God confounds the wise?
questions.explanation: The use of irony is evident in 1 Corinthians 1:27, as God uses what is deemed foolish to confound the wise, subverting expectations.

questions.question: Which Bible passage connects to the theme of God choosing the weak things of the world as seen in 1 Corinthians 1:27?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:5 states, 'Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth', echoing the idea of God valuing the humble and weak.

questions.question: Which passage parallels the concept of glorying in the Lord as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 1:31?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:23-24 emphasizes that one should not boast in wisdom or might but in knowing the Lord, aligning with 1 Corinthians 1:31.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 1 Corinthians 1:30?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:29 precedes 1 Corinthians 1:30, setting the context regarding glorying in God's presence.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 1:18, what is the preaching of the cross to those who perish?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:18 states, 'For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness...', highlighting the perception of the cross by the unsaved.

questions.question: What is stated in 1 Corinthians 1:21 about the world's wisdom?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:21 mentions, 'the world by wisdom knew not God...', indicating the limitations of human wisdom in knowing the divine.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 1:17, Paul was sent to baptize.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:17 states, 'For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel...', indicating that Paul's primary mission was preaching, not baptizing.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Corinthians 1:30, Christ is described as our redemption.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:30 states, 'who of God is made unto us... redemption...', confirming that Christ is indeed our redemption.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 1:9 teach about God's relationship to believers?
options: God is faithful and calls believers into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ
God predestines all believers to salvation without their response
God's grace is given only to those who perfectly obey the law
God is distant but allows human free will to initiate fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: God is faithful and calls believers into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:9 states, 'God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.' This teaches God's faithfulness and the calling into fellowship with Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 1:30 teach about the nature of salvation in Christ?
options: In Christ we receive wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption from God
Salvation is earned through human wisdom and righteous deeds
Christ is only a moral example for believers to follow
Redemption is a future event unrelated to present sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: In Christ we receive wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption from God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:30 states, 'But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption,' showing the multifaceted work of salvation in Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 1:18 teach about the preaching of the cross?
options: The preaching of the cross is the power of God to save those who believe
The cross is a mere symbol without saving power
Salvation comes through intellectual acceptance of wisdom rather than the cross
The cross is only a stumbling block to all people, including believers
questions.correctAnswer: The preaching of the cross is the power of God to save those who believe
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:18 explains, 'For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God,' emphasizing the cross as God's saving power.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 1:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:8 states that God 'shall also confirm you unto the end,' demonstrating God's faithfulness to preserve believers blameless.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 1:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 Corinthians 1:21 says, 'it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe,' demonstrating God's sovereign choice in salvation.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 1:10 connect to the broader biblical theme of unity in the body of Christ?
options: It calls believers to speak the same thing and avoid divisions, fulfilling Jesus' prayer for unity
It emphasizes individualism over corporate unity
It permits doctrinal divisions to express spiritual maturity
It mandates uniformity of opinion over love
questions.correctAnswer: It calls believers to speak the same thing and avoid divisions, fulfilling Jesus' prayer for unity
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:10 urges believers 'that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you,' echoing Jesus’ call for unity in John 17.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 1:22-23 relate to the redemptive-historical theme of Christ as both stumbling block and wisdom?
options: It illustrates how Christ crucified is a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Greeks, fulfilling prophecy about the Messiah’s reception
It teaches that Christ is universally accepted without offense
It denies Christ’s wisdom and power, emphasizing human ability
It suggests Christ is only relevant to one ethnic group
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates how Christ crucified is a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Greeks, fulfilling prophecy about the Messiah’s reception
questions.explanation: Verses 1 Corinthians 1:22-23 highlight that Christ crucified is offensive to Jews and Greeks, fulfilling the theme of the Messiah as a divisive figure prophesied in Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 1:26 and 1 Corinthians 1:27 teach about God’s choice in salvation?
options: God chooses the weak and foolish to shame the wise and mighty
God chooses only the elite and wise to be saved
Human wisdom and strength determine election
God’s choice is arbitrary without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God chooses the weak and foolish to shame the wise and mighty
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:26-27 shows God’s sovereign election of the weak and foolish to confound the mighty and wise, underscoring grace over human merit.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 1:4 and 1 Corinthians 1:5 teach about spiritual gifts and grace?
options: Grace enriches believers in utterance and knowledge, confirming Christ’s testimony
Spiritual gifts are earned by works of the law
Grace is unrelated to knowledge or speech
Utterance and knowledge are human achievements without divine origin
questions.correctAnswer: Grace enriches believers in utterance and knowledge, confirming Christ’s testimony
questions.explanation: Verses 1 Corinthians 1:4-5 highlight that grace given by Jesus enriches believers in speech and knowledge, confirming the truth of Christ in them.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 1:13 and 1 Corinthians 1:17 teach about the nature of Christian unity and ministry focus?
options: Christ is not divided, and ministry is to preach the gospel, not to focus on baptism or eloquence
Division is inevitable and baptism is the central ministry
Paul’s baptismal role is the foundation of unity
Human wisdom enhances the gospel's power
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is not divided, and ministry is to preach the gospel, not to focus on baptism or eloquence
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:13 and 1:17 emphasize that Christ is not divided, and Paul’s mission was preaching, not baptism or persuasive speech, to preserve the gospel’s power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 1 Corinthians 1:18-21 promotes foolishness and rejects wisdom. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches that God’s wisdom surpasses human wisdom, using what the world considers foolish to save believers
It encourages believers to reject all human knowledge
It denies any value to divine wisdom
It claims that wisdom is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God’s wisdom surpasses human wisdom, using what the world considers foolish to save believers
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:18-21 explains that God destroys worldly wisdom and uses the 'foolishness' of preaching to save, showing divine wisdom’s superiority.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 1:29 teach about human boasting before God?
options: No flesh should glory in God's presence
Human boasting is encouraged as a sign of faith
Boasting is acceptable if done humbly
questions.correctAnswer: No flesh should glory in God's presence
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:29 states, 'That no flesh should glory in his presence,' teaching that all boasting is excluded before God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 1:3 particularly demonstrate in the greeting to the church?
options: Grace and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Grace and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:3 opens with 'Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ,' demonstrating God's grace and peace toward believers.

questions.question: How do 1 Corinthians 1:12 and 1 Corinthians 1:13 together teach about the cause and remedy of church divisions?
options: Divisions arise from allegiance to leaders, but Christ is not divided, calling for unity in Him alone
Divisions are theologically necessary and unresolvable
Allegiance to Paul is the true foundation for unity
Baptism in Paul’s name is a cause for division
questions.correctAnswer: Divisions arise from allegiance to leaders, but Christ is not divided, calling for unity in Him alone
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:12 shows factions based on leaders, and 1:13 corrects this by stating 'Is Christ divided?' emphasizing unity only in Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 1:7 teach about spiritual gifts and eschatology?
options: Believers are enriched in gifts and await the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ
Spiritual gifts will cease before Christ’s return
The coming of Christ is unrelated to spiritual gifts
Only certain gifts are valid until Christ returns
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are enriched in gifts and await the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:7 says believers 'come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,' linking gifts to eschatological hope.
